components.note: 车 (cart) — 车 is a cart; 辈 first meant rows of war carts, hence ranks and generations.
非 (fēi) — near sound — 辈 is bèi; 非 also sounds out 悲 bēi and 排 pái.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他这辈子都没离开过这个小镇。
example.pinyin: Tā zhè bèizi dōu méi líkāi guò zhège xiǎozhèn.
example.english: He has never left this small town in his whole life.
example.fact: 辈子 almost always appears after a demonstrative — 这辈子 ("this lifetime"), 上辈子 ("a previous life," in a reincarnation sense), 下辈子 ("the next life") — rarely standing completely alone, since the word's whole job is to frame a span of time relative to one particular life.

examples.hanzi: 我这辈子最难忘的就是那次旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhè bèizi zuì nánwàng de jiùshì nà cì lǚxíng.
examples.english: The most unforgettable thing in my life is that trip.

examples.hanzi: 你这辈子有什么梦想？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè bèizi yǒu shénme mèngxiǎng?
examples.english: What dreams do you have in your life?

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 紧急出口在这边。
example.pinyin: Jǐnjí chūkǒu zài zhèbiān.
example.english: The emergency exit is this way.
example.fact: 出口 splits into two logically connected but very different-feeling uses: literally "mouth of exit" for a physical doorway out of a building, and figuratively the same "going-out point" for goods leaving a country (to export) — the mirror-image word 进口 ("entrance" / "to import") extends the same in/out logic on both sides at once.

examples.hanzi: 请问出口在哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn chūkǒu zài nǎr?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the exit?

examples.hanzi: 地铁站有四个出口。
examples.pinyin: Dìtiězhàn yǒu sì ge chūkǒu.
examples.english: The subway station has four exits.

components.note: 工 (work) — a left hand 𠂇 with 工 (work): the hand that helps with work; compare 右 on the right.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.hanzi: 邮局就在银行的左边。
example.pinyin: Yóujú jiù zài yínháng de zuǒbian.
example.english: The post office is right on the left side of the bank.
example.fact: 边 as a suffix turns a direction into a location noun — 左 ("left") plus 边 gives "the left side," the same pattern behind 右边 ("right side"), 上边 ("above"), and 里边 ("inside"), a small, productive family of location words all built the same way.

examples.hanzi: 书店在你的左边。
examples.pinyin: Shūdiàn zài nǐ de zuǒbian.
examples.english: The bookstore is on your left.

examples.hanzi: 他习惯用左边的手写字。
examples.pinyin: Tā xíguàn yòng zuǒbian de shǒu xiě zì.
examples.english: He is used to writing with his left hand.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 炸, 热; 爆 is to burst in flames.
暴 (bào) sounds exactly like 爆, and means violent.

example.hanzi: 气球爆了。
example.pinyin: Qìqiú bào le.
example.english: The balloon burst.
example.fact: 爆 also has slang uses: 爆满 (completely packed), 爆火 (to go viral) and 爆款 (a hit product). In cooking, 爆炒 means to stir-fry quickly over a very high flame.

examples.hanzi: 新年的时候大家放爆竹。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián de shíhou dàjiā fàng bàozhú.
examples.english: At New Year everyone sets off firecrackers.

examples.hanzi: 这家店太火爆了,要排很久的队。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn tài huǒbào le, yào pái hěn jiǔ de duì.
examples.english: This shop is so popular that you have to queue for a long time.

meanings: to hold up on the palm

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: 托 is to hold up with the hand.
乇 (tuō) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 他用手托着下巴。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu tuō zhe xiàba.
example.english: He rests his chin on his hand.
example.fact: 托 means to support something from beneath with your palm: 托盘 (tray). It also builds 委托 (to entrust), 托福 (the TOEFL exam, also 'thanks to your good fortune') and 拜托, a polite way to ask for a favor.

examples.hanzi: 他托朋友带了一本书。
examples.pinyin: Tā tuō péngyou dài le yì běn shū.
examples.english: He asked a friend to bring a book.

examples.hanzi: 服务员用托盘端来两杯茶。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán yòng tuōpán duān lái liǎng bēi chá.
examples.english: The waiter brought two cups of tea on a tray.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 警方还不清楚这起案件的动机。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng hái bù qīngchǔ zhè qǐ ànjiàn de dòngjī.
example.english: Police still aren't clear on the motive for this case.
example.fact: 机 ranges in meaning from "machine" (机器) to "opportunity" (机会) to, here, the more abstract "mechanism, trigger." 动机 reads almost literally as "the mechanism that sets something moving" — a fittingly mechanical image for whatever drives a person's actions.

examples.hanzi: 你做这件事的动机是什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò zhè jiàn shì de dòngjī shì shénme?
examples.english: What is your motive for doing this?

examples.hanzi: 学习动机很重要，要不然很难坚持。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí dòngjī hěn zhòngyào, yàobùrán hěn nán jiānchí.
examples.english: Motivation to study is important; otherwise it's hard to keep going.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.
手 (hand) — two hands joined in respect: bowing and saluting; compare 扌 in 拿 and 打.

example.hanzi: 下个礼拜我要去北京出差。
example.pinyin: Xià ge lǐbài wǒ yào qù Běijīng chūchāi.
example.english: Next week I have a business trip to Beijing.
example.fact: 礼拜 originally named the ritual of religious worship (礼, "rite," plus 拜, "to bow, to pay respects"). Because Christian services were traditionally held on Sunday, 礼拜 became colloquial shorthand for "Sunday" and then, by extension, for the whole seven-day "week" — a drift similar to how English "holiday" traces back to "holy day."

examples.hanzi: 这个礼拜五我们去看电影吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lǐbài wǔ wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
examples.english: Let's go see a movie this Friday.

examples.hanzi: 上个礼拜我感冒了，一直在家休息。
examples.pinyin: Shàng ge lǐbài wǒ gǎnmào le, yìzhí zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.english: I had a cold last week and rested at home the whole time.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — marks insects and small creatures, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蜜 honey, 蛇 snake; 蛇 is the snake.
它 (tā) — loose sound hint (shé vs tā); 它 was once a picture of a snake.

example.hanzi: 我很怕蛇。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn pà shé.
example.english: I am very afraid of snakes.
example.fact: 蛇 is the sixth animal of the Chinese zodiac and counts with the measure word 条 (一条蛇). The idiom 画蛇添足, 'draw a snake and add feet', warns against spoiling something by adding unnecessary extras.

examples.hanzi: 森林里有一条大蛇。
examples.pinyin: Sēnlín li yǒu yì tiáo dà shé.
examples.english: There is a big snake in the forest.

examples.hanzi: 他被蛇吓得跳了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi shé xià de tiào le qǐlái.
examples.english: He was so scared by a snake that he jumped.

components.note: 北 (north; two people back to back) — in older Chinese 乖 meant 'at odds, contrary' (乖张), which fits two figures turned away; 'well-behaved' is the later colloquial sense.
千 (thousand) — sits on top. Memory aid: no reliable etymology; picture a child with a thousand reasons to misbehave who still stays put.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子很乖。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn guāi.
example.english: This child is very well-behaved.
example.fact: 乖 is the praise parents give children and pets who listen: 乖孩子, 真乖. It is also an affectionate way to call out 乖 (good girl, good boy). In older Chinese it meant 'contrary, at odds' (乖僻), the reverse of today's use.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝今天特别乖。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao jīntiān tèbié guāi.
examples.english: The baby is especially well-behaved today.

examples.hanzi: 乖,快去睡觉吧。
examples.pinyin: Guāi, kuài qù shuìjiào ba.
examples.english: Be a good boy, go to sleep now.

components.note: 灬 (fire dots) — fire and heat: 热, 点, 煮, 照; 黑 is soot and smoke from a flame.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 他穿了一件黑色的外套。
example.pinyin: Tā chuān le yí jiàn hēisè de wàitào.
example.english: He wore a black coat.
example.fact: 色 attaches to almost any basic color character to spell out its full name — 黑色 ("black"), 红色 ("red"), 白色 ("white") — but dropping 色 and using the bare color character alone (黑, 红, 白) is also grammatical and common, especially right before a noun, so learners see both forms constantly with no hard rule for which one to reach for.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢黑色的鞋子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan hēisè de xiézi.
examples.english: I like black shoes the best.

examples.hanzi: 夜晚的天空是黑色的。
examples.pinyin: Yèwǎn de tiānkōng shì hēisè de.
examples.english: The night sky is black.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
口 (mouth) — calling and speech: 吗, 喊, 呼; 叫 is to shout.
丩 (jiū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 纠 jiū.

example.hanzi: 他名叫李明。
example.pinyin: Tā míngjiào Lǐ Míng.
example.english: He is named Li Ming.
example.fact: 名叫 is a slightly more written or formal way to introduce a name than the everyday spoken 叫 alone — 他叫李明 works just as well and is far more common in conversation — so 名叫 shows up more often in narration, biographies, and written introductions.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅名叫“老北京”。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng míngjiào "Lǎo Běijīng".
examples.english: This restaurant is called "Old Beijing."

examples.hanzi: 我有一只小猫，名叫豆豆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yì zhī xiǎo māo, míngjiào Dòudou.
examples.english: I have a kitten named Doudou.

components.note: 欠 (open mouth) — 欠 shows an open mouth, as in 吹, 歌, 欢; 欺 is deceiving by speech.
其 (qí) — near sound — 欺 is qī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑 ride, 驾; 骗 first meant to jump on a horse.
扁 (biǎn) — near sound — 骗 is piàn; 扁 also sounds out 偏 piān, 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.

example.hanzi: 他欺骗了所有相信他的人。
example.pinyin: Tā qīpiàn le suǒyǒu xiāngxìn tā de rén.
example.english: He deceived everyone who trusted him.
example.fact: 骗 alone already means "to trick, to swindle." Its 马 (horse) component is a fossil of the character's original sense, "to spring up onto a horse" — a sudden, unexpected leap — later extended figuratively to catching someone off guard with a trick. 欺骗 reinforces that with 欺 ("to take advantage of, to bully").

examples.hanzi: 你为什么要欺骗我？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme yào qīpiàn wǒ?
examples.english: Why do you want to deceive me?

examples.hanzi: 不要被广告上的话欺骗了。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào bèi guǎnggào shang de huà qīpiàn le.
examples.english: Don't be deceived by what the ads say.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — oldest form: a person bending over a basin of water to see a reflection; 鉴 jiàn (mirror) adds metal. To look closely, to supervise.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding the reins.
空 (kōng) is a close sound clue for kòng; 空 also in 腔 qiāng and 孔 kǒng.

example.hanzi: 这条街上到处都装了监控摄像头。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shàng dàochù dōu zhuāng le jiānkòng shèxiàngtóu.
example.english: Surveillance cameras have been installed all over this street.
example.fact: 监控 frequently doubles as a noun for the surveillance equipment itself, not just the abstract act of monitoring — 装监控 ("to install monitoring/cameras") and 看监控 ("to check the surveillance footage") are both everyday phrases where 监控 stands in for "the camera system," much like English "security" can mean both the concept and the guard.

examples.hanzi: 公司门口安装了监控设备。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī ménkǒu ānzhuāng le jiānkòng shèbèi.
examples.english: Monitoring equipment was installed at the company entrance.

examples.hanzi: 医生正在监控病人的心跳。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng zhèngzài jiānkòng bìngrén de xīntiào.
examples.english: The doctor is monitoring the patient's heartbeat.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 手机突然发出了奇怪的声音。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī tūrán fāchū le qíguài de shēngyīn.
example.english: The phone suddenly made a strange sound.
example.fact: 发出 pairs with almost any noun describing something radiating outward from a source — sound (声音), light (光), smell (气味), or a formal notice (通知) — functioning as a general-purpose "to emit / to issue" verb wherever English would reach for something more specific, like "to make," "to give off," or "to send."

examples.hanzi: 他向大家发出了邀请。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng dàjiā fāchū le yāoqǐng.
examples.english: He sent out an invitation to everyone.

examples.hanzi: 天花板上发出了一阵响声。
examples.pinyin: Tiānhuābǎn shang fāchū le yí zhèn xiǎngshēng.
examples.english: A burst of noise came from the ceiling.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 拍 is clapping or patting with the hand, also used for filming and taking photos.
白 (bái) — loose hint — 拍 is pāi; 白 also sounds out 伯 bó and 怕 pà.
灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.

example.hanzi: 我们在长城上拍照了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài Chángchéng shàng pāizhào le.
example.english: We took photos on the Great Wall.
example.fact: 拍照 is a verb-object compound built from 拍 ("to strike, to tap" — the motion of pressing a shutter) plus 照 ("to shine, to photograph"). Because the object 照 is already baked into the verb, 拍照 cannot take a further object the way English "to photograph something" can — naming a subject requires a separate phrase, like 给...拍照 ("to take a photo of...").

examples.hanzi: 请帮我们拍照，好吗？
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒmen pāizhào, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Could you take a picture of us, please?

examples.hanzi: 这里不能拍照，请把手机收起来。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù néng pāizhào, qǐng bǎ shǒujī shōu qǐlái.
examples.english: You can't take photos here, so please put your phone away.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舟 is the boat radical, as in 般, 航, 舰; 船 is a ship.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 船上有三百多名乘客。
example.pinyin: Chuánshàng yǒu sānbǎi duō míng chéngkè.
example.english: There are more than three hundred passengers on board the ship.
example.fact: 上 as a suffix after a place noun regularly means "on / at / in [that place]" — 船上 ("on the boat"), 桌上 ("on the table"), 车上 ("in the car") — one of Mandarin's most reliable location-building patterns, needing no preposition the way English "on," "at," and "in" would each have to be chosen separately.

examples.hanzi: 船上的人都穿着救生衣。
examples.pinyin: Chuán shang de rén dōu chuān zhe jiùshēngyī.
examples.english: Everyone on the ship was wearing a life jacket.

examples.hanzi: 我们在船上吃了晚饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài chuán shang chī le wǎnfàn.
examples.english: We had dinner on the boat.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 is a hole, as in 空, 窗, 突; 穿 is to pierce through, and the 牙 is a tooth boring in.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 我们穿过了一条又长又黑的隧道。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chuānguò le yì tiáo yòu cháng yòu hēi de suìdào.
example.english: We passed through a long, dark tunnel.
example.fact: 穿 alone already covers both "to wear (clothing)" and "to pierce, to pass through." 穿过 isolates and reinforces just the second, physical sense with 过 ("to cross over"), giving a verb specifically for moving through or across something — a tunnel, a crowd, or a forest.

examples.hanzi: 火车穿过一片大森林。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē chuānguò yí piàn dà sēnlín.
examples.english: The train passed through a large forest.

examples.hanzi: 过马路时，要快点穿过去。
examples.pinyin: Guò mǎlù shí, yào kuài diǎn chuān guòqù.
examples.english: When crossing the road, cross quickly.

components.note: 并 (combine) — simplified from 並, which showed two figures standing side by side; hence together, also, and (并且).
非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.

example.hanzi: 他说的话并非事实。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà bìngfēi shìshí.
example.english: What he said is by no means the truth.
example.fact: 并非 is a more emphatic, written-register stand-in for a plain 不是 ("is not"). The 并 adds a note of "contrary to what you might assume," so 并非 often appears right after a claim the speaker wants to correct or push back against — a rhetorical flavor a bare 不是 doesn't carry.

examples.hanzi: 这并非他的本意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bìngfēi tā de běnyì.
examples.english: This was not what he really meant.

examples.hanzi: 成功并非偶然，而是努力的结果。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng bìngfēi ǒurán, ér shì nǔlì de jiéguǒ.
examples.english: Success is not by chance but the result of hard work.

components.note: 彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得, 德; 彼 points out that, the other.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same part in 披 pī, 被 bèi, 破 pò.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 彼得是我在美国认识的朋友。
example.pinyin: Bǐdé shì wǒ zài Měiguó rènshi de péngyou.
example.english: Peter is a friend I met in America.
example.fact: 彼得 is a phonetic transliteration built purely for its sound — 彼 (bǐ) and 得 (dé) contribute nothing of the name "Peter"'s original meaning (from Greek petros, "rock"). This sound-first strategy is standard for foreign personal names rendered in Chinese, unlike native Chinese words, where the characters' own meanings usually matter.

examples.hanzi: 彼得每天骑自行车上班。
examples.pinyin: Bǐdé měi tiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
examples.english: Peter rides a bicycle to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天给彼得打了个电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān gěi Bǐdé dǎ le ge diànhuà.
examples.english: I called Peter yesterday.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 作. 做 is a later variant of 作 zuò (to do), sharing its meaning and sound.
故 (gù) is only a loose sound hint.
友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.

example.hanzi: 医生说,怀孕期间做爱通常是安全的。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō, huáiyùn qījiān zuò'ài tōngcháng shì ānquán de.
example.english: The doctor said that having sex during pregnancy is usually safe.
example.fact: 做爱 mirrors the English idiom "to make love" closely enough — 做 ("to do, to make") plus 爱 ("love") — that some learners assume one phrase was translated directly from the other; the two may simply have arisen independently, since "do/make + love" is a fairly natural image to reach for in more than one language.

examples.hanzi: 成年人之间做爱应该建立在互相尊重的基础上。
examples.pinyin: Chéngniánrén zhījiān zuò'ài yīnggāi jiànlì zài hùxiāng zūnzhòng de jīchǔ shang.
examples.english: Sex between adults should be based on mutual respect.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影里有做爱的镜头，不适合孩子看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǒu zuò'ài de jìngtóu, bú shìhé háizi kàn.
examples.english: This movie has a sex scene, so it isn't suitable for children.

meanings: to study at the same school

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 我们是大学同学。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì dàxué tóngxué.
example.english: We're college classmates.
example.fact: 同学 does double duty as both a noun ("classmate") and, in spoken Mandarin, a generic form of address for a student whose name you don't know — a teacher or stranger can call out "同学!" much like English might use "excuse me" toward a young person on campus.

examples.hanzi: 我们是高中同学，认识十年了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì gāozhōng tóngxué, rènshi shí nián le.
examples.english: We are high school classmates and have known each other for ten years.

examples.hanzi: 同学们，请打开书，翻到第五页。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen, qǐng dǎkāi shū, fān dào dìwǔ yè.
examples.english: Students, please open your books and turn to page five.

meanings: abbr. for 阿非利加洲[A1 fei1 li4 jia1 Zhou1]

components.note: 非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 洲 is land surrounded by water.
州 (zhōu) — same sound — 洲 is zhōu, like 州; continents like 亚洲 are 洲.

example.hanzi: 他去非洲旅行了三个月。
example.pinyin: Tā qù Fēizhōu lǚxíng le sān gè yuè.
example.english: He traveled around Africa for three months.
example.fact: 洲 is the dedicated character for "continent" and attaches to a single root syllable for each of the world's continents — 非洲 (Africa), 亚洲 (Asia), 欧洲 (Europe), 美洲 (the Americas) — all built the same transparent way, unlike English's unrelated continent names.

examples.hanzi: 非洲有很多美丽的草原和野生动物。
examples.pinyin: Fēizhōu yǒu hěn duō měilì de cǎoyuán hé yěshēng dòngwù.
examples.english: Africa has many beautiful grasslands and wild animals.

examples.hanzi: 非洲的夏天比我们这里热得多。
examples.pinyin: Fēizhōu de xiàtiān bǐ wǒmen zhèlǐ rè de duō.
examples.english: Summers in Africa are much hotter than here.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.

example.hanzi: 空袭警报响了,大家都躲进了地下室。
example.pinyin: Kōngxí jǐngbào xiǎng le, dàjiā dōu duǒ jìn le dìxiàshì.
example.english: The air raid alarm went off, and everyone hid in the basement.
example.fact: 报 by itself means "to report, to announce" (as in 报纸, "newspaper," literally "report-paper") — 警报 combines it with 警 ("to warn, to alert") to mean, quite literally, "a warning announcement," the same logic behind 警察 ("police," literally "alert-observe").

examples.hanzi: 火警警报突然响了，大家马上离开了大楼。
examples.pinyin: Huǒjǐng jǐngbào tūrán xiǎng le, dàjiā mǎshàng líkāi le dàlóu.
examples.english: The fire alarm suddenly went off and everyone left the building right away.

examples.hanzi: 手机收到了暴雨警报。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī shōudào le bàoyǔ jǐngbào.
examples.english: My phone received a heavy rain alert.

meanings: (of a batter) to be put out (in baseball)
(of a player or team) to be eliminated from a competition

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.

example.hanzi: 这支球队在半决赛中出局了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì zài bànjuésài zhōng chūjú le.
example.english: This team was eliminated in the semifinals.
example.fact: 出局 borrows its core image from baseball and other turn-based games, where 局 means "a round, an inning" — so 出局 literally means "to go out of the round." A sports term for "eliminated," it has since spread into everyday talk about competitions, job cuts, and even politics.

examples.hanzi: 他今天状态不好，第一轮就出局了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān zhuàngtài bù hǎo, dì-yī lún jiù chūjú le.
examples.english: He was off today and got knocked out in the first round.

examples.hanzi: 这个球员因为犯规被罚出局。
examples.pinyin: Zhège qiúyuán yīnwèi fànguī bèi fá chūjú.
examples.english: This player was sent off for a foul.

components.note: 内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 这份文件只在公司内部流传。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn zhǐ zài gōngsī nèibù liúchuán.
example.english: This document only circulates within the company.
example.fact: 内部 pairs 内 ("inside") with 部 ("section, department, part") to describe not just physical interiors but organizational ones too — 内部消息 ("inside information"), 内部矛盾 ("internal conflict") — a natural extension from physical space to institutional structure.

examples.hanzi: 这个会议只限公司内部人员参加。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huìyì zhǐ xiàn gōngsī nèibù rényuán cānjiā.
examples.english: Only internal company staff may attend this meeting.

examples.hanzi: 手机的内部结构很复杂。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī de nèibù jiégòu hěn fùzá.
examples.english: The internal structure of a phone is very complicated.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买; 质 is the real value or substance of something.

example.hanzi: 劫机者扣留了机上所有乘客作为人质。
example.pinyin: Jiéjīzhě kòuliú le jī shàng suǒyǒu chéngkè zuòwéi rénzhì.
example.english: The hijacker held all the passengers on the plane hostage.
example.fact: 质 can mean "pledge, guarantee" as well as "quality, substance" — its 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) component is a fossil of that older "valuable pledge" sense. 人质 keeps this ancient meaning nearly intact: literally "a person held as a pledge," almost unchanged from the character's root meaning thousands of years on.

examples.hanzi: 警察成功救出了人质。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá chénggōng jiù chū le rénzhì.
examples.english: The police successfully rescued the hostages.

examples.hanzi: 那些人质被关了两天才获救。
examples.pinyin: Nàxiē rénzhì bèi guān le liǎng tiān cái huòjiù.
examples.english: The hostages were held for two days before being rescued.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 请等我一会,我马上就回来。
example.pinyin: Qǐng děng wǒ yíhuì, wǒ mǎshàng jiù huílái.
example.english: Please wait for me a moment, I'll be right back.
example.fact: 一会 is often doubled into 一会儿一会儿 ("now this, now that") to describe rapid back-and-forth changes, as in 天气一会儿晴一会儿雨 ("the weather keeps swinging between sunny and rainy") — the same short-duration word repurposed to frame quick alternation, not just a single brief interval.

examples.hanzi: 我想休息一会，再继续工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiūxi yíhuì, zài jìxù gōngzuò.
examples.english: I want to rest a while before continuing to work.

examples.hanzi: 你先坐一会，饭马上就好。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò yíhuì, fàn mǎshàng jiù hǎo.
examples.english: Sit for a bit; the meal will be ready soon.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 扮 is to dress or act.
分 (fēn) — loose hint — 扮 is bàn; 分 also sounds out 盼 pàn.
氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.

example.hanzi: 她在这部电影里扮演一位老师。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ bànyǎn yí wèi lǎoshī.
example.english: She plays a teacher in this movie.
example.fact: 扮 alone means "to dress up as, to disguise oneself as" (as in 打扮, "to get dressed up"), and 演 alone means "to perform, to act out." 扮演 combines "costuming" with "performing" into one verb, where English splits the same idea across "to play (a role)" and "to portray."

examples.hanzi: 他在话剧里扮演一个年轻的医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huàjù lǐ bànyǎn yí ge niánqīng de yīshēng.
examples.english: He plays a young doctor in the stage play.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢扮演自己崇拜的英雄。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan bànyǎn zìjǐ chóngbài de yīngxióng.
examples.english: Children like to play the heroes they admire.

components.note: 北 — two people (匕) back to back; the meaning "north" is a later loan, and "back" survives in the reading bèi (败北 defeat).

example.hanzi: 北京在中国的北方。
example.pinyin: Běijīng zài Zhōngguó de běifāng.
example.english: Beijing is in the north of China.
example.fact: 北 began as two people back to back and gave the sense 'to turn one's back', as in 败北 (to be defeated). It also came to mean 'north', since buildings traditionally faced south with their backs to the north.

examples.hanzi: 超市在学校的北边。
examples.pinyin: Chāoshì zài xuéxiào de běibian.
examples.english: The supermarket is north of the school.

examples.hanzi: 冬天北方比南方冷多了。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān běifāng bǐ nánfāng lěng duō le.
examples.english: In winter the north is much colder than the south.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 姿 first meant a woman's bearing.
次 (cì) — near sound — 姿 is zī; 次 also sounds out 资 zī and 咨 zī.
力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 势 is force or momentum.

example.hanzi: 瑜伽老师纠正了我的姿势。
example.pinyin: Yújiā lǎoshī jiūzhèng le wǒ de zīshì.
example.english: The yoga teacher corrected my posture.
example.fact: 姿势 refers to a concrete physical posture — how a body is positioned in space, as in exercise or photos — while its near-synonym 姿态 leans more abstract, covering overall bearing, stance, or attitude (political 姿态, for instance) as well as physical carriage.

examples.hanzi: 坐在电脑前，你的姿势要正确。
examples.pinyin: Zuò zài diànnǎo qián, nǐ de zīshì yào zhèngquè.
examples.english: When you sit at the computer, your posture should be correct.

examples.hanzi: 他摆了一个很帅的姿势让我拍照。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎi le yí ge hěn shuài de zīshì ràng wǒ pāizhào.
examples.english: He struck a cool pose for me to take a photo.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服很漂亮。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn piàoliang.
example.english: This piece of clothing is very pretty.
example.fact: 服 appears in 衣服 (clothes), 服务 (service), 服从 (to obey), 舒服 (comfortable), 佩服 (to admire) and 服药 (to take medicine). In 衣服 the second syllable is a neutral tone, fu.

examples.hanzi: 这条裤子我穿着很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi wǒ chuān zhe hěn shūfu.
examples.english: These pants are very comfortable to wear.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的服务很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de fúwù hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The service at this restaurant is very good.

components.note: 糸 (silk thread; 纟 on the left) — ties and connections, as in 红, 给, 经. 系 is a link or relation.

example.hanzi: 他在大学的历史系教书。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué de lìshǐ xì jiāoshū.
example.english: He teaches in the university's history department.
example.fact: 系 xì is the word for a university department (中文系, 历史系), and builds 系统 (system), 关系 (relationship) and 联系 (contact). Read jì, it means to tie: 系鞋带 (tie shoelaces), 系领带 (tie a tie).

examples.hanzi: 我是中文系的学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì Zhōngwén xì de xuésheng.
examples.english: I am a student in the Chinese department.

examples.hanzi: 这两件事没有关系。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn shì méiyǒu guānxi.
examples.english: These two things are unrelated.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室, 安; 宇 is the eaves, then all that is under heaven.
于 (yú) — near sound — 宇 is yǔ; 于 also sounds out 芋 yù.
宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室, 安; 宙 together with 宇 forms 宇宙, space and time.
由 (yóu) — near sound — 宙 is zhòu; 由 also sounds out 抽 chōu and 袖 xiù.

example.hanzi: 科学家一直在研究宇宙的起源。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā yìzhí zài yánjiū yǔzhòu de qǐyuán.
example.english: Scientists have been studying the origin of the universe.
example.fact: 宇 originally named the eaves of a house — the outer edge of a bounded space — while 宙 referred to the passage of time within that same dwelling; 宇宙 fuses the two into "all of space" plus "all of time," an image that maps naturally onto the modern physics notion of spacetime, centuries before the term existed in Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 宇宙中有数不清的星星。
examples.pinyin: Yǔzhòu zhōng yǒu shǔ bù qīng de xīngxing.
examples.english: There are countless stars in the universe.

examples.hanzi: 我从小就对宇宙充满好奇。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóngxiǎo jiù duì yǔzhòu chōngmǎn hàoqí.
examples.english: I have been full of curiosity about the universe since I was little.

components.note: 目 (eye) — marks the eyes and seeing, as in 看 look, 睛 eye, 盯 stare; 瞎 is blind, with 害 adding harm.
害 (hài) — loose sound hint (xiā vs hài); same part in 割 gē and 辖 xiá.

example.hanzi: 别瞎说!
example.pinyin: Bié xiā shuō!
example.english: Don't talk nonsense!
example.fact: 瞎 literally means blind, but it is more often an adverb for doing something with no basis: 瞎说 (talk nonsense), 瞎猜 (guess wildly), 瞎忙 (be busy for nothing). 瞎子 for a blind person is considered impolite; 盲人 is neutral.

examples.hanzi: 别瞎忙了,先休息一下。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiā máng le, xiān xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: Stop busying yourself for nothing and rest a bit.

examples.hanzi: 我瞎猜的,不一定对。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiā cāi de, bù yídìng duì.
examples.english: I just guessed randomly, so it may not be right.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.

example.hanzi: 她明天要去参加一个面试。
example.pinyin: Tā míngtiān yào qù cānjiā yí gè miànshì.
example.english: She has a job interview to attend tomorrow.
example.fact: 面试 (literally "face test") is paired with 笔试 ("pen test," a written exam) as the two-part vocabulary Chinese uses to distinguish an in-person interview from a written test — both compounds share 试, the character for "to try, to test."

examples.hanzi: 面试的时候不要紧张。
examples.pinyin: Miànshì de shíhou bú yào jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: Don't be nervous during the interview.

examples.hanzi: 我上周面试了三家公司。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shàng zhōu miànshì le sān jiā gōngsī.
examples.english: Last week I interviewed with three companies.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 三点水 marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 酒 liquor, 河 river; 汤 is soup or hot water.
昜 (yáng) — near sound — 汤 is tāng; 昜 also sounds out 扬 yáng, 场 chǎng, 烫 tàng.

example.hanzi: 这碗汤很好喝。
example.pinyin: Zhè wǎn tāng hěn hǎohē.
example.english: This bowl of soup is very tasty.
example.fact: In Chinese meals, 汤 is often drunk alongside the food rather than served as a starter. 汤圆 are sweet glutinous rice balls in a soup, traditionally eaten at the Lantern Festival. The classical sense 'hot water' survives in the idiom 赴汤蹈火, 'go through fire and water'.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈给我煮了一碗鸡汤。
examples.pinyin: Māma gěi wǒ zhǔ le yì wǎn jītāng.
examples.english: Mom made me a bowl of chicken soup.

examples.hanzi: 先喝点热汤吧,暖暖身体。
examples.pinyin: Xiān hē diǎn rè tāng ba, nuǎnnuan shēntǐ.
examples.english: Have some hot soup first to warm up.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.
斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.

example.hanzi: 这是这个品牌最新的手机型号。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì zhège pǐnpái zuìxīn de shǒujī xínghào.
example.english: This is the brand's latest phone model.
example.fact: 最 functions as Mandarin's all-purpose superlative marker — stuck directly onto almost any adjective (最好 "best," 最大 "biggest," 最新 "newest") — doing the job that English splits between the suffix "-est" and the separate word "most."

examples.hanzi: 这是最新的天气预报。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zuìxīn de tiānqì yùbào.
examples.english: This is the latest weather forecast.

examples.hanzi: 你看过他最新的电影吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn guo tā zuìxīn de diànyǐng ma?
examples.english: Have you seen his latest movie?

components.note: 臣 (eye) — 臣 is a picture of an eye looking down; with a person leaning, 卧 is lying down.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 他家有两个卧室。
example.pinyin: Tā jiā yǒu liǎng gè wòshì.
example.english: His home has two bedrooms.
example.fact: 卧室 literally means "lying-down room" — 卧 pictures a person reclining, and 室 is a roofed, enclosed chamber — a transparent compound that singles out the bedroom specifically, in contrast to the generic 房间 ("room") that covers any room in the house.

examples.hanzi: 我们的卧室在二楼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de wòshì zài èr lóu.
examples.english: Our bedroom is on the second floor.

examples.hanzi: 他把卧室打扫得干干净净。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ wòshì dǎsǎo de gāngān-jìngjìng.
examples.english: He cleaned the bedroom until it was spotless.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and distance, as in 过, 近, 进: 远 is a road that goes far.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuǎn; 元 also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他远离辛辣的食物。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā yuǎnlí xīnlà de shíwù.
example.english: The doctor advised him to stay away from spicy food.
example.fact: 远离 works as a transitive verb — 远离 + object — for both physical and figurative distance ("stay away from spicy food," "get away from your phone"), a construction the plain adjective 远 ("far") can't form on its own, since 远 needs a coverb like 离 to attach to a following noun.

examples.hanzi: 这家工厂远离市区，空气很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng yuǎnlí shìqū, kōngqì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This factory is far from the city, and the air is good.

examples.hanzi: 小朋友要远离危险的地方。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎopéngyou yào yuǎnlí wēixiǎn de dìfang.
examples.english: Children should stay away from dangerous places.

components.note: 丽 (beautiful) — simplified 麗, which showed a deer 鹿 with antlers, a symbol of grace. Seen in 美丽.

example.hanzi: 这里的风景很美丽。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měilì.
example.english: The scenery here is beautiful.
example.fact: 丽 almost always appears in compounds: 美丽 (beautiful), 华丽 (gorgeous), 秀丽 (graceful). It is a very common element in given names, such as 丽丽 and 美丽. The simplified 丽 is not related in shape to 鹿 any more, though the traditional form is.

examples.hanzi: 海边的日落真美丽。
examples.pinyin: Hǎibiān de rìluò zhēn měilì.
examples.english: The sunset by the sea is really beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 她穿着华丽的裙子。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe huálì de qúnzi.
examples.english: She is wearing a gorgeous dress.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的剧本改编自一本小说。
example.pinyin: Zhèbù diànyǐng de jùběn gǎibiān zì yì běn xiǎoshuō.
example.english: This movie's screenplay is adapted from a novel.
example.fact: 本 alone can mean "book," "edition," or the measure word for bound volumes (一本书), and 剧本 literally reads as "the drama's book" — the written text a play, film, or TV series is built from, the same 本 pattern behind 课本 ("textbook") and 日记本 ("diary").

examples.hanzi: 他正在写一个电视剧的剧本。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài xiě yí ge diànshìjù de jùběn.
examples.english: He is writing the script for a TV drama.

examples.hanzi: 演员们正在背剧本，准备明天的演出。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnyuánmen zhèngzài bèi jùběn, zhǔnbèi míngtiān de yǎnchū.
examples.english: The actors are memorizing their scripts to prepare for tomorrow's show.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and asking: 说, 谢, 谈; 请 is to ask politely.
青 (qīng) sounds like 请 (tone differs); same part in 清, 情, 晴, 精, 静.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 请问,洗手间在哪里?
example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, xǐshǒujiān zài nǎlǐ?
example.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
example.fact: 请问 is a fixed opening formula — it always precedes a question, never a statement — functioning like English "excuse me, but..." or "may I ask..." to politely address a stranger before asking directions, a favor, or information.

examples.hanzi: 请问，你叫什么名字？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?
examples.english: Excuse me, what is your name?

examples.hanzi: 请问去火车站怎么走？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
examples.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.

example.hanzi: 小孩用手指指着天上的月亮。
example.pinyin: Xiǎohái yòng shǒuzhǐ zhǐzhe tiānshàng de yuèliang.
example.english: The child pointed at the moon in the sky with their finger.
example.fact: 指 does double duty as both a noun meaning "finger" and a verb meaning "to point" — sensible since pointing is literally done with a finger — so 手指 (the noun "finger") and 指 (the verb "to point," as in 指着 "pointing at") share the same root character.

examples.hanzi: 他的手指被门夹住了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǐ bèi mén jiā zhù le.
examples.english: His finger got caught in the door.

examples.hanzi: 她的手指又细又长，很适合弹钢琴。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǐ yòu xì yòu cháng, hěn shìhé tán gāngqín.
examples.english: Her fingers are slender and long, perfect for playing the piano.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 皿 is a dish or container, as in 盘 plate, 盖 cover, 益; 盒 is a box.
合 (hé) — same sound — 盒 is hé, matching 合; 合 also sounds out 哈 hā.

example.hanzi: 这个盒子里有什么?
example.pinyin: Zhège hézi lǐ yǒu shénme?
example.english: What's in this box?
example.fact: 盒 is a small box with a lid, as in 饭盒 (lunch box), 文具盒 (pencil case) and 盒饭 (boxed meal). It doubles as a measure word, 一盒巧克力 (a box of chocolates). A large box is 箱 (xiāng).

examples.hanzi: 请给我一个饭盒。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge fànhé.
examples.english: Please give me a lunch box.

examples.hanzi: 桌子上放着一盒巧克力。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang fàng zhe yì hé qiǎokèlì.
examples.english: There is a box of chocolates on the table.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.hanzi: 警方已经证实了这个消息。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng yǐjīng zhèngshí le zhège xiāoxi.
example.english: The police have already confirmed this piece of news.
example.fact: 证实 specifically means to verify that a claim or report is objectively true, often through evidence or investigation — common in news and police contexts — while its near-synonym 确认 leans toward administrative confirmation, like confirming a booking or acknowledging receipt of a message.

examples.hanzi: 这份报告证实了我们的想法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào zhèngshí le wǒmen de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: This report confirmed our idea.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息还没有得到证实。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi hái méiyǒu dédào zhèngshí.
examples.english: This news has not yet been confirmed.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech and exclamations, as in 啊, 呀, 哦; 哎 is a cry of surprise.
艾 (ài) hints at the sound: 哎 āi is close.

example.hanzi: 哎,你的手机在这儿!
example.pinyin: Āi, nǐ de shǒujī zài zhèr!
example.english: Hey, your phone is right here!
example.fact: 哎 is used to get someone's attention or to express mild surprise or regret. 哎呀 is a stronger 'oh no/oh my', and 哎哟 reacts to pain or surprise. Tones can vary with the mood, so pitch carries emotion here.

examples.hanzi: 哎呀,我忘了带钥匙!
examples.pinyin: Āiyā, wǒ wàng le dài yàoshi!
examples.english: Oops, I forgot to bring my keys!

examples.hanzi: 哎,别哭了,没事的。
examples.pinyin: Āi, bié kū le, méishì de.
examples.english: Hey, don't cry, it's all right.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进; 迈 is a big stride.
万 (wàn) — near sound — 迈 is mài, from the traditional 邁 where 萬 gave the sound.
阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 阿 first meant a slope.
可 (kě) — near sound — 阿 is ā; 可 also sounds out 河 hé and 哥 gē.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.

example.hanzi: 他们计划明年去迈阿密旅行。
example.pinyin: Tāmen jìhuà míngnián qù Mài'āmì lǚxíng.
example.english: They are planning to travel to Miami next year.
example.fact: 迈阿密 is a pure phonetic transliteration of the English "Miami" — 迈 ("to stride"), 阿 (a meaningless filler syllable common across transliterated foreign names, as in 阿富汗 "Afghanistan"), and 密 ("dense, secret") are borrowed only for their sounds, not their meanings, the same strategy behind virtually all foreign place names in Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 迈阿密的冬天也很暖和。
examples.pinyin: Mài'āmì de dōngtiān yě hěn nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: Even winter in Miami is warm.

examples.hanzi: 他在迈阿密有一套海边的房子。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Mài'āmì yǒu yí tào hǎibiān de fángzi.
examples.english: He has a house by the sea in Miami.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.

example.hanzi: 祝你一路平安!
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yílù píng'ān!
example.english: Wishing you a safe journey!
example.fact: 一路 anchors a whole family of travel farewells — 一路平安 ("safe travels") and 一路顺风 ("smooth journey," literally "wind at your back the whole way") — the fixed phrases Chinese speakers reach for when seeing someone off on a trip.

examples.hanzi: 我们一路上都在聊天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yílù shang dōu zài liáotiān.
examples.english: We chatted all the way.

examples.hanzi: 你也去机场吗？那我们正好一路。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yě qù jīchǎng ma? Nà wǒmen zhènghǎo yílù.
examples.english: Are you going to the airport too? Then we are going the same way.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买; 资 is capital or resources.
次 (cì) is a loose clue; same part in 姿 zī and 咨 zī.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 他没有参加这次考试的资格。
example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu cānjiā zhècì kǎoshì de zīgé.
example.english: He doesn't have the qualifications to take this exam.
example.fact: 资格 shows up constantly in the pattern 有/没有...的资格 ("to have/not have the standing to...") — used for formal eligibility, like exam qualifications, but just as often rhetorically, as in 你没有资格说这话 ("you have no right to say that").

examples.hanzi: 你有资格参加这个比赛。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu zīgé cānjiā zhège bǐsài.
examples.english: You are qualified to take part in this competition.

examples.hanzi: 他在这家公司工作了十年，资格很老。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhè jiā gōngsī gōngzuò le shí nián, zīgé hěn lǎo.
examples.english: He has worked at this company for ten years and has a lot of seniority.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and swimming, as in 河, 海, 泳: swimming and drifting.
斿 (yóu) gives the exact sound: a flag with streamers that floats freely.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢在海里游泳。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài hǎi lǐ yóuyǒng.
example.english: I like swimming in the sea.
example.fact: 游 covers both 'swim' and 'roam': 游泳 (to swim), 旅游 (to travel), 游客 (tourist), 游戏 (game). The idea in both senses is moving freely, floating or wandering without a fixed route.

examples.hanzi: 暑假我们去云南旅游。
examples.pinyin: Shǔjià wǒmen qù Yúnnán lǚyóu.
examples.english: We're traveling to Yunnan this summer.

examples.hanzi: 他游泳游得比我快。
examples.pinyin: Tā yóuyǒng yóu de bǐ wǒ kuài.
examples.english: He swims faster than I do.
